raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Add opt-in parallel diagonal solves and fused zero stores to the existing
non-TMA GDN 64x64 inverse. The default solver remains unchanged.

## Claims

- Batch the four independent 16x16 diagonal recurrences, preserving the existing
  block-merge algorithm and IEEE dot products.
- Initialize unwritten upper blocks and varlen padding in the same launch,
  avoiding the separate zero-fill launch.
- Restrict the opt-in path to FP32 inputs, BF16 outputs, B=1, H=32, BT=64,
  variable lengths and non-TMA execution; other configurations retain the
  original implementation.

## Validation

Base: `4bd75e952a9f423742223c97c8cc9fc6db362950`.
Candidate: `be22e9878d7c47459bc860ac771895d4d610d4cf`.

[Raw measurements, model outputs and reproduction scripts](https://github.com/rowanbyte/vllm/tree/c550/gdn-port-evidence-20261019/validation/gdn-port-20261019)
are retained separately from the proposed code diff.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Inverse/reference values, upper zeros, padding, fallback and changed-length CUDA graph replay | 13 passed, 2.63 s |
| Real Qwen3.5-35B-A3B W8A8 regression | 8/8 greedy token sequences identical; candidate eligible path executed 210 times |
| Changed-file pre-commit, mypy, test tethering, signoff, Python 3.12 compile check and diff check | Passed |

Five alternating baseline/candidate pairs, 100 eager wrapper calls per sample
after 10 warmups, CUDA-event timing on MetaX C550:

| Active tokens | Baseline median ms (min-max) | Candidate median ms (min-max) | Median latency reduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1072 | 0.111557 (0.111114–0.111721) | 0.075761 (0.073306–0.075960) | 32.09% |
| 3216 | 0.330168 (0.329480–0.332733) | 0.169592 (0.167841–0.169697) | 48.63% |

These are eager solver-call measurements, not whole-model TPM gains. Other
workers were resident during timing; this was not an exclusive-device study.
An initial graph attempt stalled while creating a CUDA stream, before kernel
capture. After releasing a completed idle experiment, the full graph test passed.
Two model-test setup failures in RPC serialization were fixed before inference;
they are retained in local records and excluded from successful validation.

**Execution scope:** the exact new solver source was loaded with the pinned
MetaX engine's FLA dependencies. GPU tests used Python 3.10.10, MetaX Torch
`2.10.0+metax3.8.0.7` and vendor Triton 3.6.0. Static checks used a separate
Python 3.12.15 environment. This was not a complete build or serving validation
of current upstream main. NVIDIA/ROCm performance and official accuracy scores
are not claimed.

The real-model overlay used TP1, eager mode, no MTP, prefix caching disabled,
temperature 0, seed 20261008 and max_tokens 128. Self-contained cases covered
arithmetic, geography, Chinese, JSON and 1316/5156-token prompts. All output
tokens matched; all seven cases with explicit expected answers passed on both
sides. This is a functional regression check, not an accuracy benchmark.

Reproduce in a compatible installed upstream GPU environment:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/fla/test_solve_tril.py -v
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_gdn_solve_tril.py \
  --lengths 1072 3216 --repeats 5 --timing event
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/solve_tril.py \
  tests/kernels/fla/test_solve_tril.py \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_gdn_solve_tril.py
```

These are intended upstream reproduction commands. The linked evidence explains
the different source-overlay procedure actually used for local GPU validation.

## Details

Enable with `FLA_TRIL_PARALLEL_DIAGONALS=1`. No model weights, quantization,
sampling settings, core scheduler or model runner interfaces are changed.
Register/layout effects may vary by accelerator, so the path remains opt-in.

### Duplicate-work check

Refreshed open-PR searches for `solve_tril` and the author's parallel-inverse PRs
found no existing PR implementing this standalone diagonal/zero-store change.

- [#38315](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38315) fuses KKT, inverse
  and WY preparation. This change keeps those interfaces and optimizes the
  existing standalone inverse instead; it does not add another KKT/WY fusion.
- [#61779](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61779) targets GDN prefill
  metadata and grids, rather than the inverse recurrence and initialization.

AI assistance was used for implementation, duplicate-work research, tests,
benchmark automation and this description. The human submitter confirmed review
of the change before publication. The test results above were produced with
AI assistance; no separate human-run test result is asserted here.

@@ -0,0 +1,93 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Compare opt-in GDN inverse fusion with the original varlen solver."""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import os
+import statistics
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops.solve_tril import solve_tril
+from vllm.triton_utils import triton
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--lengths", type=int, nargs="+", default=[1072, 3216])
+    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=5)
+    parser.add_argument("--timing", choices=["graph", "event"], default="graph")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if args.repeats < 1 or any(length < 1 for length in args.lengths):
+        parser.error("Positive lengths and repeat count are required")
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    results = []
+    for length in args.lengths:
+        a = torch.randn((1, length + 16, 32, 64), device="cuda") * 0.01
+        rows = torch.arange(length + 16, device="cuda") % 64
+        columns = torch.arange(64, device="cuda")
+        a.masked_fill_(columns[None, None, None, :] >= rows[None, :, None, None], 0)
+        a[:, length:] = 0
+        cu = torch.tensor([0, length], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+        indices = torch.tensor(
+            [(0, i) for i in range(triton.cdiv(length, 64))],
+            device="cuda",
+            dtype=torch.int32,
+        )
+        samples = {"baseline": [], "candidate": []}
+        outputs = {}
+        for trial in range(args.repeats):
+            order = ["baseline", "candidate"]
+            if trial % 2:
+                order.reverse()
+            for variant in order:
+                os.environ["FLA_TRIL_PARALLEL_DIAGONALS"] = (
+                    "1" if variant == "candidate" else "0"
+                )
+
+                def invoke(a=a, cu=cu, indices=indices):
+                    return solve_tril(a, cu, indices, torch.bfloat16)
+
+                outputs[variant] = invoke()
+                if args.timing == "graph":
+                    milliseconds = triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph(invoke)
+                else:
+                    start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+                    end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+                    for _ in range(10):
+                        invoke()
+                    start.record()
+                    for _ in range(100):
+                        invoke()
+                    end.record()
+                    end.synchronize()
+                    milliseconds = start.elapsed_time(end) / 100
+                samples[variant].append(milliseconds)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            outputs["candidate"], outputs["baseline"], atol=2e-3, rtol=2e-3
+        )
+        baseline = statistics.median(samples["baseline"])
+        candidate = statistics.median(samples["candidate"])
+        results.append(
+            {
+                "length": length,
+                "samples_ms": samples,
+                "baseline_median_ms": baseline,
+                "candidate_median_ms": candidate,
+                "latency_reduction_percent": 100 * (1 - candidate / baseline),
+            }
+        )
+    print(
+        json.dumps(
+            {
+                "device": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
+                "timing": args.timing,
+                "results": results,
+            }
+        )
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Check inverse values, untouched padding, and graph replay for varlen GDN."""
+
+import importlib
+from itertools import accumulate
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+solve_module = importlib.import_module(
+    "vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops.solve_tril"
+)
+
+
+def make_inputs(lengths, padding=16, heads=32):
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    capacity = sum(lengths) + padding
+    a = torch.zeros((1, capacity, heads, 64), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    chunks = []
+    start = 0
+    for seq, length in enumerate(lengths):
+        for offset in range(0, length, 64):
+            n = min(64, length - offset)
+            values = torch.randn((heads, n, n), device="cuda") * 0.02
+            a[0, start + offset : start + offset + n, :, :n] = torch.tril(
+                values, diagonal=-1
+            ).permute(1, 0, 2)
+            chunks.append((seq, offset // 64))
+        start += length
+    cu = torch.tensor([0, *accumulate(lengths)], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    indices = torch.tensor(chunks[::-1], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    return a, cu, indices
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "lengths", [[1], [15], [16], [17], [33], [49], [63], [64], [65, 79], [3216]]
+)
+def test_parallel_inverse_preserves_values_and_zero_padding(monkeypatch, lengths):
+    if solve_module.is_tma_supported:
+        pytest.skip("The opt-in implementation excludes TMA")
+    a, cu, indices = make_inputs(lengths)
+    monkeypatch.setenv("FLA_TRIL_PARALLEL_DIAGONALS", "0")
+    expected = solve_module.solve_tril(a, cu, indices, torch.bfloat16)
+    monkeypatch.setenv("FLA_TRIL_PARALLEL_DIAGONALS", "1")
+    actual = solve_module.solve_tril(a, cu, indices, torch.bfloat16)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=2e-3, rtol=2e-3)
+    assert torch.count_nonzero(actual[:, sum(lengths) :]).item() == 0
+    start = 0
+    for length in lengths:
+        for offset in range(0, length, 64):
+            n = min(64, length - offset)
+            result = actual[0, start + offset : start + offset + n].permute(1, 0, 2)
+            assert torch.count_nonzero(torch.triu(result, diagonal=1)).item() == 0
+            matrix = a[0, start + offset : start + offset + n, :, :n].permute(1, 0, 2)
+            identity = torch.eye(n, device=a.device).expand(32, n, n)
+            reference = torch.linalg.solve_triangular(
+                matrix + identity, identity, upper=False
+            )
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                result[:, :, :n].float(), reference, atol=2e-3, rtol=2e-3
+            )
+        start += length
+
+
+def test_parallel_inverse_graph_replay_uses_current_lengths(monkeypatch):
+    if solve_module.is_tma_supported:
+        pytest.skip("The opt-in implementation excludes TMA")
+    a, cu, indices = make_inputs([65, 79], padding=0)
+    monkeypatch.setenv("FLA_TRIL_PARALLEL_DIAGONALS", "1")
+    solve_module.solve_tril(a, cu, indices, torch.bfloat16)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        actual = solve_module.solve_tril(a, cu, indices, torch.bfloat16)
+    changed, changed_cu, changed_indices = make_inputs([65, 78], padding=1)
+    a.copy_(changed)
+    cu.copy_(changed_cu)
+    indices.copy_(changed_indices)
+    graph.replay()
+    monkeypatch.setenv("FLA_TRIL_PARALLEL_DIAGONALS", "0")
+    expected = solve_module.solve_tril(a, cu, indices, torch.bfloat16)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=2e-3, rtol=2e-3)
+    assert torch.count_nonzero(actual[:, 143:]).item() == 0
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("heads,dtype", [(24, torch.bfloat16), (32, torch.float32)])
+def test_parallel_option_preserves_unsupported_configurations(
+    monkeypatch, heads, dtype
+):
+    a, cu, indices = make_inputs([17, 65], heads=heads)
+    monkeypatch.setenv("FLA_TRIL_PARALLEL_DIAGONALS", "0")
+    expected = solve_module.solve_tril(a, cu, indices, dtype)
+    monkeypatch.setenv("FLA_TRIL_PARALLEL_DIAGONALS", "1")
+    actual = solve_module.solve_tril(a, cu, indices, dtype)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=0, rtol=0)
